routes.name: Residence permit for a self-employed person
Registration of an EU citizen with the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs

note: Latvia. The Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs' own site (pmlp.gov.lv) didn't answer from here on 2026-10-30 (no connection), so the file was written on secondary sources stating its rules, read that day and again on 2026-11-03: the European Commission's EU Immigration Portal pages 'Employed worker in Latvia' and 'Self-employed worker in Latvia', and the Spanish Embassy in Riga's page on EU citizens. On 2026-11-03 the Office's own pages answered: a residence permit is needed to stay over 90 days in half a year, and its state fee table (updated 18 March 2026, under Cabinet Regulation No. 731 of 26 November 2024) prices the review of a temporary residence permit's documents at 160 euros within 30 days (280 within 10 working days, 560 within 5). The EU Immigration Portal's 100 euros (200 and 400) were older than that regulation: the fee written was 100 until 2026-11-03 and is 160 since, the ordinary review with its 30 days as the decision time. The registration of the permit once granted (75 euros within 30 days) and the residence permit card (45 euros) are further fees, not added. A third-country worker needs the State Employment Agency's vacancy test, then the employer's invitation approved by the Office, after which the person applies at a Latvian diplomatic or consular mission abroad (abroad). The permit is granted for the period of employment 'but not longer than five years' (a ceiling, so no term is kept) and is registered and renewed every year (renewable). 'Right to work is tied to a specific position and a specific employer' (work for the sponsor). The self-employed apply at a mission abroad for a permit granted 'for up to one year' (no term kept), renewable while the activity goes on and a set tax (9,960 euros a year) has been paid, at the same review fee; it 'allows access to any additional self-employed activity', which isn't the form's any work, so work is left out. Long-term resident status may be granted after at least five years' legal residence (5 kept as both permits' years to it), with means, Latvian and a residence; its holder has 'no restrictions to work' (any); the Office's table prices the review for EU long-term resident status at 160 euros within 30 days (written with its 30 days, 2026-11-03); where it is asked isn't on these pages. These terms, the work rights and the five years are the Portal's, not yet read on the Office's site. EU citizens may live in Latvia without a residence permit and register with the Office for stays over 90 days in a half-year (the Spanish Embassy's page, for Spaniards as EU citizens; whether EEA and Swiss citizens are the same isn't said there, so only the EU is named); what work registration allows isn't said there, so work is left out. Naturalisation isn't read here.

sources.title: European Commission, EU Immigration Portal, Employed worker in Latvia
sources.said: If you want to be admitted as a worker to reside in Latvia for a period longer than 90 days within half a year counting from the first day of entrance, you must obtain a temporary residence permit. ... Once the employer’s invitation is approved, a person can apply for a residence permit at the diplomatic or consular representative of the Republic of Latvia abroad. ... up to 30 days – 100 euros, ... The residence permit is granted for the period of employment but not longer than five years. ... Residence permit should be registered and renewed every year. ... Right to work is tied to a specific position and a specific employer. Changes are not allowed. ... A long-term resident status may be granted if you have resided legally in the Republic of Latvia for at least five years. ... If you have a long-term resident status, you have no restrictions to work in the Republic of Latvia.

sources.title: European Commission, EU Immigration Portal, Self-employed worker in Latvia
sources.said: Applications are submitted to a ... diplomatic or consular representative office of the Republic of Latvia abroad ... up to 30 days - 100 euros, ... Residence permits for self-employment are granted for up to one year. ... A third-country citizen can renew a residence permit if self-employed activities are still being carried out and if during the previous period of residence certain tax amount has been paid to the budget (9960 euros per year). ... The residence permit allows access to any additional self-employed activity. ... A long-term resident status may be granted if you have resided legally in the Republic of Latvia for at least five years

sources.title: Embajada de España en Riga, Documentación y trámites
sources.said: Los españoles, como ciudadanos de la Unión Europea,  pueden residir en Letonia sin necesidad de una autorización de residencia. Si su duración se prevé superior a los 90 días por semestre, deberá registrarse en el Departamento de Ciudadanía y Migración de Letonia.

sources.title: PMLP, Residence Permits (updated 02.12.2025)
sources.said: A residence permit is necessary if you are willing to reside in the Republic of Latvia for a period of time exceeding 90 days within half a year counting from the first day of entrance.
